Competitor News.title: At Barclays Center, a new look emerges with art, clubs and the cloud
Competitor News.summary: At Barclays Center, a new look emerges with art, clubs and the cloud NetsDaily
Competitor News.copy:
Barclays Center looked different when Brooklyn Nets fans arrived for Opening Night Wednesday, their first game since look on April 9. On one level, it’s part of yet another upgrade at the arena but on another level, it’s different. It’s not just brick-and-mortar improvement at entrances, better ingress and egress or a new club (or two.) It’s about art and cloud technology and an immersive in-house experience to pull fans away from the comfort of their own home and into the Nets own space.

Some of it is temporary, some is permanent but all of it was quite visible … and visual. The most noteworthy addition is temporary, but will make appearances throughout the season, but it certainly qualifies as art. The Nets 60th anniversary court, dressed up in ABA colors, was striking and it included a feature that blew a lot of minds. Around the edges of the court were the names of all 575 players who ever donned one of the Nets many uniforms going back to the New Jersey Americans. There was Brook Lopez who holds the career record for points as well as Wenyen Gabriel who played one game as a COVID replacement.

Wider Sports News.title: SPFL tender could end Saturday 3pm TV blackout but is it really under threat?
Wider Sports News.summary: Scottish soccer league says it is ‘flexible’ about how many matches it makes available to broadcasters but doesn’t necessarily mean restrictions will end. And if they do, will Premier League and EFL follow suit? The post SPFL tender could end Saturday 3pm TV blackout but is it really under threat? appeared first on SportsPro .
bullets: The Scottish Professional Football League has issued a tender for its media cycle beginning with the 2029/30 season, offering broadcasters the chance to show every match live, which would end the 3pm Saturday blackout. Its current Sky Sports deal is worth £150m over four years, with up to 60 fixtures a year shown, alongside a secondary deal with Premier Sports for 22 live games a season.

The SPFL has said it is flexible on how many matches it makes available, and bidders could still opt against a model including 3pm fixtures. Only 36 per cent of top-flight matches are currently available to watch in the UK. Any move to scrap the blackout would need the cooperation of the English Football League, and the Premier League has said it is committed to the blackout beyond its current cycle.
Wider Sports News.copy:
The Scottish Professional Football League (SPFL) is offering broadcasters the opportunity to broadcast every single one of its matches live in a move that would end the traditional 3pm blackout that prevents live soccer from airing on UK television on Saturday afternoons.

The league, which represents the top four divisions of Scottish soccer, has issued a tender for its next media cycle which begins with the 2029/30 season. Its current deal with Sky Sports is worth UK£150 million (US$162 million) over a four-year period, with the pay-TV broadcaster airing up to 60 fixtures a year.

Wider Sports News.title: AFA expands Genius Sports deal for semi-automated offside
Wider Sports News.summary: AFA expands Genius Sports deal for semi-automated offside Sportcal
bullets: Argentina's AFA has renewed and expanded its partnership with Genius Sports, introducing semi-automated offside technology across every Primera División game using the GeniusIQ platform, supported by automated visuals for TV coverage. The agreement begins with the 12 December Torneo Clausura final and will ramp up through next year ahead of the July kick-off of the Torneo Clausura 2027.

The two first partnered in 2019 on betting integrity services, and in 2021 the deal grew to cover betting data and live streaming rights across all 13 AFA-run competitions. GeniusIQ combines tracking, video and insights, and also powers real-time advertising activations and augmented broadcasts. AFA president Claudio Tapia said Genius has launched the most advanced such system in world football, while the firm said the deal creates a foundation for further innovation.
Wider Sports News.copy:
Argentine soccer’s AFA governing body has renewed and expanded its partnership with prominent sport technology firm Genius Sports, a move that will introduce ‘semi-automated offside’ systems to the domestic top-flight Primera División.

The expanded partnership will see the AFA leverage Genius Sports’ GeniusIQ offering to institute semi-automated offside tech (SAOT) across every Primera División game, supported by automated visuals for TV coverage.

Both said they were terminating all cooperation with the Real Madrid and France forward with immediate effect.

Wider Sports News.copy:
Kylian Mbappe was dropped Tuesday by two major brands in China after a video circulated online in which the French football star apparently joked about former leader Mao Zedong.

In China jokes about Mao, the country's founding leader who died in 1976, are considered disrespectful and remain a social taboo. "Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments," drinks giant Dongpeng said in a statement, adding that "with immediate effect we are terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappe".

It also represents a 57% increase in MLB team sponsorship value between 2022 ($1.35B) and 2026, with total deals up 17% over that span (3,195 to 3,732).

The average MLB team sponsorship deal size is $590,000, up 5.9% YOY. Two teams heading to new ballparks led in sponsorship revenue growth: the Rays (33.8% YOY increase) and the Athletics (19.3% YOY increase). The Dodgers, who last year became the first team in North American pro sports to surpass $200M in annual sponsorship revenue (14.5% YOY increase), the White Sox (14.5% YOY increase) and the Mariners (10.2% YOY increase) rounded out the top-five.

Wider Sports News.title: South Africa opts for Durban as preferred 2036 Olympics host city

bullets: The South African Olympic Committee has named Durban as its preferred main candidate city to host the Summer Olympic and Paralympic Games in 2036 or 2040, which would be the first Olympics held in Africa. Acting president Lwandile Simelane said the bid will probably include some events in other locations. Johannesburg and Cape Town were also considered, and the Moses Mabhida Stadium, built for the 2010 FIFA World Cup, would be the centrepiece.

South Africa is one of seven countries to have confirmed 2036 bids, alongside Germany, Hungary, Turkiye, Qatar, India and South Korea. The IOC has set a deadline of 31 October for declaring interest. A shortlist is due next March, preferred hosts will be named in 2028 and the final decision is expected in 2029. Durban was stripped of the 2022 Commonwealth Games for failing to provide guarantees, and Cape Town last bid for the 2004 Games.
Wider Sports News.copy:

Wider Sports News.copy:
There are some sponsorship deals that arrive at just the right time. Sprite was the official soft drink of the National Basketball Association (NBA) from 1994 to 2015. It had been involved with the league since 1986, but this bigger partnership launched as Sprite began setting out a new brand identity. Early in the sports drink boom and with another skirmish unfolding in the cola wars, it drew on Gen X irony and irreverence to give consumers a simpler call to action.

Its ‘obey your thirst’ pitch – the digested message of which was ‘ignore the noise, this lemon-lime drink is refreshing’ – used knowing and zeitgeisty humour to carve a slice of the counterculture for a brand owned by Coca-Cola.

bullets: The US Justice Department has opened an inquiry into whether the National Football League breached antitrust rules in its television deals and then required customers to pay too much in subscription costs, according to three sources familiar with the probe. The Wall Street Journal first reported the investigation, and the Justice Department declined to comment.

The Sports Broadcasting Act of 1961 gives the NFL limited protection to pool broadcast rights. The NFL said its model is the most fan and broadcaster-friendly in the industry, with over 87% of games on free broadcast television, and noted that the 2025 season was its most viewed since 1989. Senator Mike Lee, who chairs the Senate antitrust subcommittee and had urged the inquiry, said games placed behind subscription paywalls may no longer align with the Act's rationale.

Wider Sports News.title: Experts call for alcohol sponsorship ban after Scotland World Cup exposure study
Wider Sports News.summary: Experts call for alcohol sponsorship ban after Scotland World Cup exposure study The Herald
bullets: Academics at the University of Stirling, Dr Richard Purves and Dr Catherine Best, have called on the Scottish Government to consider comprehensive restrictions on alcohol sports sponsorship. Their study, funded by Scottish Health Action on Alcohol Problems (SHAAP), analysed 30-second broadcast intervals across Scotland's World Cup matches and found alcohol advertising in almost a quarter of them. Alcohol branding was more prevalent during the matches themselves than in commercial breaks.

SHAAP chair Dr Alastair MacGilchrist said viewers saw alcohol branding around every two minutes, and that self-regulation has not protected children and young people. He urged the government to set out restrictions and a timetable in its alcohol harm prevention plan, due this year. He cited France, which has banned alcohol sports sponsorship for more than 30 years, and noted that most Scottish Premiership clubs have alcohol-industry sponsors or partnerships.
Wider Sports News.copy:
Leading academics have called upon the Scottish Government to consider comprehensive restrictions on alcohol sports sponsorship, after a study revealed the extent to which young people and children were exposed to alcohol advertising during Scotland’s World Cup campaign.

The research, which was funded by Scottish Health Action on Alcohol Problems and undertaken by Dr Richard Purves and Dr Catherine Best of the University of Stirling, analysed 30-second broadcast intervals across Scotland matches, and found that alcohol advertising was present in almost a quarter of them, including frequent exposure to alcohol marketing throughout match coverage.

Bids are due by midnight on 19 November, with a FIFA delegation to meet media companies in the United States around Thanksgiving and a winner expected before the end of 2026. bullets: World Rugby has confirmed two changes to tackle laws ahead of the Autumn Internationals, targeting hip-drop and knee-drop techniques. Hip-drop tackles will be explicitly outlawed under Law 9.13 from 1 November, with offenders facing at least a penalty and yellow or red cards possible for more dangerous incidents.

Guidance on knee-drop tackles, which were already covered by existing laws, took effect on 5 October, with officials told to enforce them more consistently. World Rugby chairman Brett Robinson said the evidence showed hip-drop tackles, although rare, could cause significant leg injuries, and that knee-drop tackles were on the rise. The changes follow research commissioned after February's Shape of the Game meeting, and the amendment was approved on 28 September and announced on 7 October.
Rugby.copy:
World Rugby has confirmed two changes to tackle laws ahead of the Autumn Internationals, with new rules coming into force this weekend. The governing body has moved to crack down on dangerous tackling techniques, with hip-drop and knee-drop tackles both targeted.

The changes come just days before England, Scotland, Wales and Ireland begin their November campaigns. Players could now face penalties, yellow cards or red cards for tackles that previously lacked specific guidance.

Rugby.title: PREM Rugby report major change in financial health of clubs
Rugby.summary: PREM Rugby revenues have beaten forecasts by £7.8 million as the league reported improving finances across all 10 clubs ahead of the 2026/27 season.
bullets: PREM Rugby revenues in the 2025 financial year came in £7.8m above forecast, according to the league's second annual Financial Monitoring Report, with a further five per cent rise projected by 2027. All 10 clubs have passed the Financial Monitoring System for 2026/27 as the league, which says it generates more than £260m, enters its 30th season.

Combined losses are forecast to fall by £26.7m between FY23 and FY27, while external debt is expected to drop 26 per cent and the number of clubs needing shareholder support to halve from eight to four. Stadium occupancy reached 82 per cent in 2025/26 and central sponsorship revenue has doubled since 2022. Investment includes Red Bull in Newcastle, Sir James Dyson's 50 per cent stake in Bath and Black Knight Rugby's takeover of Exeter.

Rugby.title: Rugby World Cup nation face World Rugby suspension with immediate effect
Rugby.summary: Rugby World Cup nation face World Rugby suspension with immediate effect Ruck.co.uk
bullets: World Rugby, the Samoan government and rugby authorities have agreed interim measures to address governance concerns at Lakapi Samoa, following tensions between the government-backed national union and Lakapi Samoa, which World Rugby supports. A Samoan-led independent review will investigate the union, while the Samoa Association of Sports and National Olympic Committee will take responsibility for high-performance rugby. Domestic competitions will continue as normal.

Lakapi Samoa has self-suspended from the World Rugby Council, which can be lifted only by a request to the World Rugby Executive Board and a recommendation to the Council. Samoa's eligibility for international competition is unaffected. Prime Minister La'auli Leuatea Schmidt withdrew his support for Lakapi Samoa three months ago and launched a rival Samoa Rugby Football Union in August. Samoa are in Pool D at the 2027 Rugby World Cup with France, Japan and the United States.
Rugby.copy:
World Rugby has released a statement following growing reports of unrest and infighting within the administration of Samoan rugby. Tensions have emerged between the Samoan government-backed national rugby union and Lakapi Samoa, which is supported by World Rugby, over the governance and future direction of the game in the Pacific nation.

World Rugby chairman Brett Robinson is currently in Apia, where he has held crisis talks with Samoa's Prime Minister La'aulialemalietoa (La'auli) Leuatea Schmidt. He has also met separately with Lakapi Samoa officials.

Rugby.title: Ireland's Furlong cleared of groin grab by disciplinary committee
Rugby.summary: Ireland's Tadhg Furlong is cleared by a disciplinary committee of grabbing Gavin Coombes in the groin during Leinster's United Rugby Championship win over Munster.
bullets: Ireland's Tadhg Furlong has been cleared by a disciplinary committee of grabbing Gavin Coombes in the groin during Leinster's 24-18 United Rugby Championship win over Munster at the Aviva Stadium. The panel unanimously dismissed the citing complaint under Law 9.27, concluding he did not commit an act of foul play.

Coombes raised the allegation with referee Andrew Brace in the first half, but television match official Colin Stanley could not find conclusive video evidence, and Furlong was later cited. The panel of Simon Thomas, Attie Heyns and Pamela Woodman said Coombes had given an honest account of his recollection. Furlong, 33, is available for Ireland's Nations Championship home matches against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa and the finals weekend fixture at Twickenham.
Rugby.copy:
Ireland's Tadhg Furlong has been cleared by a disciplinary committee of grabbing Gavin Coombes in the groin during Leinster's United Rugby Championship win over Munster. Munster back row Coombes raised the allegation with match referee Andrew Brace in the first half of Leinster's 24-18 win at Aviva Stadium, but television match official (TMO) Colin Stanley could not find conclusive video evidence.

However, three-time British and Irish Lions tourist Furlong was subsequently cited over an act of foul play under Law 9.27, which says "a player must not do anything that is against the spirit of good sportsmanship including but not limited to grabbing, twisting or squeezing the genitals".

Scotland were winless in his five WXV fixtures, losing to Canada and the Black Ferns and three times to the Wallaroos.

Rugby.title: Gareth Anscombe: 'I felt like I still had another year left in me'
Rugby.summary: It was 12 years ago this week that Gareth Anscombe first arrived in Wales amid a blaze of publicity.
bullets: Gareth Anscombe, 35, has returned to Wales with the Scarlets after leaving Bayonne at the end of the Top 14 season, in what could be the final chapter of his playing career. The former Wales fly-half won 42 caps and played in two World Cups. He made his second league appearance in last weekend's 52-40 defeat by the Stormers in Cape Town, and the Scarlets face the Bulls at Loftus Versfeld on Saturday.

Anscombe said he felt he had another year left in him and did not want to move his family much, and that Dwayne Peel approached him late in the season. He will compete for the number ten shirt with Sam Costelow, Carwyn Leggatt-Jones and Joe Hawkins. He sees his role as partly supportive, sharing experience with the squad, and said he would like to look at coaching in future.
Rugby.copy:
It was 12 years ago this week that Gareth Anscombe first arrived in Wales amid a blaze of publicity. He had come over from New Zealand to join Cardiff having been targeted by Warren Gatland after sharing in the Chiefs’ 2013 Super Rugby title triumph, starting at full-back in the final.

The Auckland-born Anscombe had represented the land of his birth at U20s level, starring at fly-half as the Kiwis won the 2011 Junior World Championship. But Gatland was aware he was qualified for Wales through his Cardiff-born mother and not tied to New Zealand.

Rugby.copy:
New Zealand Rugby (NZR) has today confirmed the direction of the country’s elite men’s rugby competition and streamlined player pathways that underpin it. Currently, Super Rugby Pacific and the NPC operate as New Zealand’s two men’s competitions, supported by 19 professional rugby environments across five Super Rugby clubs and 14 Provincial Unions.

Rugby.summary: Red Roses' star Ellie Kildunne is named on England's bench again as head coach John Mitchell makes six changes to his side to face the United States.
bullets: England head coach John Mitchell has made six changes for Friday's match against the USA in New Jersey, with full-back Ellie Kildunne again named on the bench. Kildunne, 27, was dropped for the 31-22 defeat by Canada in Ottawa last Saturday, and Emma Sing retains her place. Tatyana Heard, Claudia Moloney-MacDonald, Flo Robinson and Holly Aitchison make their first starts of the tour, while Mackenzie Carson and Maud Muir replace Hannah Botterman and Sarah Bern in the pack.

The defeat ended England's 41-match unbeaten run and was their first back-to-back losses since 2016. Mitchell said he had been expecting a dip, noting that he has introduced younger players since the World Cup triumph and wants a running threat at scrum-half in Exeter Chiefs' Robinson. Coaching consultant Shaun Edwards left the group after the Canada loss, as previously agreed, and Mitchell has been defence coach this week. The next Test is in the Women's Six Nations in six months.

Despite the loss in Ottawa, Bristol Bears star Kildunne will once again have to settle for a place on the bench for Friday's match against the USA in New Jersey, with Emma Sing retaining her spot.

Rugby.title: Prem eyes English expansion despite Welsh interest
Rugby.summary: Welsh rugby may be keen on forming an Anglo-Welsh league but the Prem and RFU are only looking at English clubs in any expansion.
bullets: Prem Rugby and the Rugby Football Union have confirmed they are focusing on expanding the Prem with English clubs rather than Welsh sides, with a provisional target of growing from 10 to 12 teams by 2029-30. The statement followed reports that the Welsh Rugby Union has expressed interest in joining an Anglo-Welsh league, although English sources say no negotiations are taking place.

Promotion and relegation has been scrapped from the start of 2026-27, with clubs instead applying to join and being judged on play, finances, investment potential, infrastructure and geography. The WRU, which posted an £18m loss last year, is committed to four URC teams until the end of 2027-28 and plans to cut to three professional sides by 2028. It is also pitching two women's teams for Premiership Women's Rugby. The Prem's "P-share" entry cost is understood to be valued at £20m.
Rugby.copy:
English rugby bosses have confirmed they are concentrating on expanding the Prem with English clubs rather than bringing in teams from Wales. Prem Rugby, which runs the English top flight, has released a joint statement alongside the Rugby Football Union (RFU) stating they were looking at adding two English clubs by 2029.

This came after reports the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) has expressed an interest in joining an Anglo-Welsh league. The Professional Rugby Board (PRB), which runs the professional game in Wales, met on Wednesday and were told the WRU plans to explore a future in the English club game.

Rugby.title: Anglo-Welsh league: Prem Rugby cool on idea despite WRU interest
Rugby.summary: Anglo-Welsh league: Prem Rugby cool on idea despite WRU interest BBC
bullets: Prem Rugby and the RFU said in a joint statement that they are focused on expanding the English top flight with English clubs, targeting two more sides to reach 12 teams by 2029-30. It follows reports that the WRU has expressed interest in joining an Anglo-Welsh league, which English sources acknowledge but say involves no negotiations. Promotion and relegation ends from 2026-27, with clubs instead applying on criteria including finances and infrastructure.

The WRU said it is committed to providing four teams to the URC until the end of 2027-28 and will decide its future men's operating model by the end of this season, while keeping other competition options under review. It posted an £18m loss for the latest year, against £7.2m the year before. The Prem's "P-share" entry cost is understood to be £20m. WRU plans to cut to three professional licences remain, with a December summit called and a final decision expected in summer 2027.

Rugby.title: Janse van Rensburg set to return in December
Rugby.summary: Bristol Bears and England centre Benhard Janse van Rensburg will have to wait until December to play again following a head injury.
bullets: Bristol Bears and England centre Benhard Janse van Rensburg is set to return to rugby in December after two serious head injuries in three months. The 29-year-old was stretchered off after being knocked unconscious in the win over Northampton on 3 October. He then left the field on a stretcher again in his second England appearance, against Argentina seven days later. He had scored on his England debut against Fiji after qualifying on residency grounds in July.

Specialists ruled him out of England's Nations Championship campaign next month. He has returned to training but is not yet cleared for contact, so he will miss Friday's Prem match against Leicester at Ashton Gate. Director of rugby Pat Lam said he will be ready for the Bath game on 4 December. Lam said the club opted for the six-week end of the 4-6 week guidance, and that the player is frustrated. Janse van Rensburg joined Bristol from London Irish in 2023 and signed a new deal earlier this month.

Beale has not played for the Wallabies since a game against Wales in Cardiff in 2021. He could win a 96th cap against England at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham, on Sunday 8 November.

Head coach Les Kiss said Beale's 95 caps bring Test experience and versatility, primarily at inside centre, and pointed to his form for Western Force. Australia then play Scotland at Murrayfield and Wales in Cardiff before finals weekend in London towards the end of November. James Ramm has also been added to the squad, and Kalani Thomas will join after Australia A commitments. Beale played at the 2011, 2015 and 2019 World Cups, and the next tournament is at home in less than a year.

Rugby.title: Injury-hit Stormers confirm capture of double world champion Mbonambi
Rugby.summary: Double World Cup winner Bongi Mbonambi has returned to the Stormers on a one-year deal.
Rugby.copy:
Double World Cup winner Bongi Mbonambi has returned to the Stormers on a one-year deal. The Springbok hooker, who made 74 appearances in his first spell with the club between 2015 and 2021, moves to Cape Town from the Sharks, after his contract there was terminated with the agreement of both parties following a disciplinary dispute.

Mbonambi is available for selection with immediate effect and is set to feature in the United Rugby Championship encounter with Ulster at DHL Stadium on Saturday. With hookers André-Hugo Venter, Deon Fourie, Lukhanyo Vokozela, Almero Keizer and Luca Bakkes all injured and JJ Kotzé currently serving a suspension, the Stormers have turned to Mbonambi to help them through a difficult period.

Rugby.title: Four World Cup winners ruled out of Springboks' Nations Championship squad
Rugby.summary: Rugby World Cup winners Cheslin Kolbe, Eben Etzebeth, Andre Esterhuizen and Handre Pollard have been ruled out of the Springboks' November tour due to injury.
bullets: Cheslin Kolbe (broken jaw), Eben Etzebeth (lower-limb), Andre Esterhuizen (ankle) and Handre Pollard (hamstring), all Rugby World Cup winners, have been ruled out of the Springboks' 37-man squad for November's Nations Championship matches. South Africa face Italy on 7 November, France on 13 November and Ireland on 21 November, before the Finals Weekend in London on 27-29 November.

Head coach Rassie Erasmus has named six uncapped players: Yaqeen Ahmed, Sebastian de Klerk, Luan Giliomee, Markus Muller, Riley Norton and Emmanuel Tshituka, all of whom have previously been involved in the Springbok set-up. Siya Kolisi remains captain. South Africa topped the Southern Series in July after beating England, Scotland and Wales. Erasmus said building squad depth is a key pillar and that the six earned their call-ups through consistent franchise form.
Rugby.copy:
Rugby World Cup winners Cheslin Kolbe, Eben Etzebeth, Andre Esterhuizen and Handre Pollard have been ruled out of the Springboks’ November tour due to injury. Erasmus has taken the opportunity to take a further look at some of the rising stars of South African rugby by naming six uncapped players in the squad. Yaqeen Ahmed, Sebastian de Klerk, Luan Giliomee, Markus Muller, Riley Norton, and Emmanuel Tshituka all earning their first national call-ups for the Boks’ last four Tests of 2026.

Rugby.title: Queensland Rugby Union and Buildcorp Finalise Three-Year Partnership Extension Through 2029
Rugby.summary: Queensland Rugby Union and Buildcorp Finalise Three-Year Partnership Extension Through 2029 Ministry of Sport
Rugby.copy:
The Queensland Rugby Union (QRU) and construction firm Buildcorp have announced a three-year extension of their commercial partnership, securing the agreement through 2029. Buildcorp will remain the principal naming-rights partner of the Buildcorp Reds Academy, continuing a multi-year sponsorship that commenced in 2022 to support elite rugby union talent pathways across Queensland.

The Buildcorp Reds Academy operates a three-tier development structure catering to more than 70 high-performance male athletes aged 16 to 20. The Academy serves as the primary player pipeline for the Queensland Reds Super Rugby Pacific squad, with athletes utilising the Ballymore-based BMS National Rugby Training Centre, a facility constructed and completed by Buildcorp in 2023.

Rugby.title: England’s Nations Championship plans hit by Pepper and Van Rensburg double blow
Rugby.summary: England’s Nations Championship plans hit by Pepper and Van Rensburg double blow The Guardian
bullets: England head coach Steve Borthwick has lost Bath flanker Guy Pepper, who has an ankle injury, and Bristol centre Benhard van Rensburg, who has been advised to rest after two heavy concussions in three months, for the whole autumn. Both are out for several weeks. Fly-half Fin Smith is doubtful with a calf problem sustained against Leicester, and it is "unclear" whether he will face Australia next week.

Borthwick plans to name the team around Wednesday for the Sunday fixture, with George Ford and Marcus Smith as fly-half alternatives. Bath hooker Kepu Tuipulotu left training with a leg injury, while Seb Atkinson and Manny Feyi-Waboso should be available for their clubs this weekend. England have lost their usual extra week of preparation because of the Nations Championship finals weekend, and only nine Tests remain before World Cup preparations enter their final stages.
Rugby.copy:
England’s head coach, Steve Borthwick, said he will be monitoring this weekend’s domestic Prem games with some trepidation. Already he has lost at least two potentially key squad members for the entire autumn period in the form of Guy Pepper and Benhard van Rensburg, with doubts still hanging over his first-choice fly-half, Fin Smith, and fresh injury uncertainty emerging on virtually a daily basis.

Pepper’s involvement always looked improbable from the moment he sustained a nasty-looking ankle injury against Gloucester last Friday. The young Bath flanker will be sidelined for several weeks, as will the Bristol centre Van Rensburg who has been advised to rest and recuperate after two heavy concussions within the past three months.

bullets: England back-row Guy Pepper has been ruled out of the Nations Championship matches against Australia, Japan and New Zealand. The 23-year-old hurt his ankle in Bath's Gallagher PREM defeat to Gloucester at Kingsholm last weekend, and Bath confirmed the news in an injury update. England return home for the Nations Championship finals weekend, where their opponents will depend on their northern hemisphere standing.

Pepper played in all five Six Nations matches, starting four, and featured in all three summer Nations Championship fixtures. He scored his first England try against Fiji in July 2026 and was Man of the Match in Bath's 2025 Premiership final win. Bath also confirmed that Santiago Carreras has ruptured an anterior cruciate ligament and is out for the season, while Dan du Preez remains unavailable. Sam Underhill is targeting an early December return and Jamie Bhatti a return in the New Year.
Rugby.copy:

Bath confirmed in an injury update that Pepper will miss England's matches against Australia, Japan and New Zealand. Steve Borthwick's side will then return to home soil for the Nations Championship finals weekend. Their opponents will depend on their final position in the northern hemisphere standings.

Rugby.title: Wales call up in-form Page after Dyer injury blow
Rugby.summary: Wales release Rio Dyer from their Nations Championship squad after hamstring injury, with Scarlets wing Macs Page added for November's games.
bullets: Dragons wing Rio Dyer has been released from the Wales squad for the Nations Championship with a hamstring injury, and uncapped Scarlets back Mac Page has been called up. Dyer, 26, was recalled by head coach Steve Tandy after a strong start to the season but was hurt scoring against Ospreys last weekend. He will rehabilitate with the Dragons. His most recent of 24 caps came against South Africa last autumn.

Page, 21, scored his fifth try of the season for the Scarlets at the Stormers last Saturday but suffered a heavy head knock and must complete return-to-play protocols before pushing for a first cap. He joins Ellis Mee, Blair Murray, Louis Rees-Zammit, Tom Rogers, Josh Adams and Gabriel Hamer-Webb as back-three options. Wales play Japan in Cardiff on Saturday 7 November, then host New Zealand and Australia, before facing another southern hemisphere side on Nations Championship finals weekend at Twickenham at the end of the month.
Rugby.copy:
Dragons wing Rio Dyer has been released from the Wales squad for the Nations Championship because of a hamstring injury, with uncapped Scarlets back Mac Page called up. Dyer was recalled by head coach Steve Tandy after a strong start to the season, but suffered an injury in the process of scoring against Ospreys last weekend.

The 26-year-old faces a spell on the sidelines and has been released to rehabilitate with the Rodney Parade club. Dyer won the most recent of his 24 caps against South Africa last autumn and missed out on the Six Nations and summer squads.

The 33-year-old is accused of grabbing Munster's Gavin Coombes by the genitals under Law 9.27, which covers acts against fair play. Bans for such offences start at 12 weeks, with the most severe cases carrying up to 208 weeks.

Coombes complained to referee Andrew Brace during the first half. The television match official, Colin Stanley, could not establish what happened from the footage, but the complaint was recorded in the referee's report and reviewed by the citing commissioner. A disciplinary panel will decide the seriousness if Furlong is found guilty. Even a 12-week ban could rule him out of the November Tests and might affect his place in the 2027 Six Nations. South Africa hooker Jan-Hendrik Wessels received a nine-week ban in 2025 for a similar act.
Rugby.copy:
Ireland star Tadhg Furlong could face a ban of up to four years after being cited following Leinster's clash with Munster. The 33-year-old prop is accused of grabbing Munster star Gavin Coombes by the genitals.

The alleged act took place during Leinster's 24-18 win on Saturday. As RUCK reported earlier, Furlong was cited on Monday. He now faces a hearing that could lead to a lengthy ban.

bullets: Ireland prop Tadhg Furlong has been cited over an alleged groin grab during Leinster's 24-18 United Rugby Championship win over Munster at the Aviva Stadium on Saturday. Munster back row Gavin Coombes raised the allegation with referee Andrew Brace in the 37th minute, but television match official Colin Stanley found no video evidence at the time. Furlong has been cited under Law 9.27, and the URC said disciplinary arrangements would be announced in due course.

If found guilty, the 33-year-old could miss Ireland's Nations Championship matches against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa in Dublin, plus the finals weekend in London. South Africa's Jan-Hendrik Wessels received a nine-match suspension in October 2025 for a similar offence, after a 12-week ban was reduced by three weeks. A comparable sanction would also rule Furlong out of Leinster's Champions Cup pool match with Sale and the festive derbies with Ulster and Munster.
Rugby.copy:

Munster back row Gavin Coombes raised the allegation against an unnamed Leinster player with match referee Andrew Brace in the closing stages of the first half at the Aviva Stadium, but television match official (TMO) Colin Stanley could not find any video evidence at the time.

However, experienced front row Furlong has now been cited over an act of foul play under Law 9.27, which says a "a player must not do anything that is against the spirit of good sportsmanship including but not limited to grabbing, twisting or squeezing the genitals".

Rugby.summary: World Rugby confirms law change – but it’s too late for injured international Ruck.co.uk
bullets: Dragons head coach Filo Tiatia has urged World Rugby to bring forward its new tackle law after a knee-drop tackle forced Tongan international Fetuli Paea off injured in the Dragons' 31-14 defeat to the Ospreys at St Helen's. Tiatia called the tackle dangerous and said Paea's condition would be assessed medically.

World Rugby confirmed a few weeks ago that knee-drop tackles will be outlawed from 1 November. The change forms part of a wider effort to reduce dangerous contact, and World Rugby has also confirmed that the hip-drop tackle is to be removed. Tiatia, a former New Zealand international, pointed to the NRL's strict approach to the technique, while the tackle on the 32-year-old Paea remains permitted under the current laws.
Rugby.copy:
Dragons RFC head coach Filo Tiatia has called on World Rugby to bring forward its new tackle law after condemning a ‘dangerous’ knee-drop tackle, which left Tongan international Fetuli Paea limping off during his side’s defeat to the Ospreys.

World Rugby confirmed only a number of weeks ago that knee-drop tackles will be outlawed by November 1, but Tiatia believes they should not wait until then to act. Paea was forced off injured in the Gwent side’s 31-14 defeat at the newly revamped St Helen’s, as Tiatia made his feelings clear following the full-time whistle.

Former England captain Courtney Lawes, also at Sale Sharks after leaving Brive, has not been recalled by Borthwick.

Rugby.title: Duhan van der Merwe stood down after just 18 minutes of comeback match
Rugby.summary: Duhan van der Merwe stood down after just 18 minutes of comeback match Ruck.co.uk
bullets: Scotland winger Duhan van der Merwe was forced off after 18 minutes of his first appearance of the season for Edinburgh against the Lions on Friday, suffering a hand injury following an aerial contest. Edinburgh had confirmed 24 hours earlier that he had recovered from a long-running ankle problem, and he was replaced by Harry Paterson.

Head coach Sean Everitt said the injury, a laceration to the hand, was unrelated to the ankle issue, though he had not yet spoken to the medics and no timescale has been given. Scotland coach Gregor Townsend is due to name his Nations Championship squad on Monday, with a match against the All Blacks on 7 November. Van der Merwe, 31, is Scotland's all-time leading men's try scorer, having overtaken Stuart Hogg's record of 27.
Rugby.copy:
Scotland star Duhan van der Merwe suffered another injury setback after lasting just 18 minutes on his return for Edinburgh. The powerful winger was making his first appearance of the season against the Lions on Friday night after recovering from a long-running ankle problem.

However, his comeback was cut short when he suffered a hand injury following an aerial contest. Van der Merwe was forced off and replaced by Harry Paterson, raising fresh concerns ahead of Scotland's November internationals.

Rugby.title: Munster's Coombes backed after making groin grab allegation
Rugby.summary: Munster head coach Clayton McMillan backs Gavin Coombes after the back row alleged he had been grabbed in the groin in Saturday's defeat by Leinster.
bullets: Munster head coach Clayton McMillan has backed number eight Gavin Coombes, who alleged he was grabbed in the groin by an unnamed Leinster player at a ruck late in the first half of Saturday's 24-18 United Rugby Championship defeat at the Aviva Stadium. Coombes raised the matter with referee Andrew Brace, but TMO Colin Stanley found no video evidence of the incident.

McMillan said he backs his players "100%" when they make such allegations and that it was now for "the powers that be", referring to the citing commissioner, who can review incidents retrospectively. Leinster head coach Leo Cullen said he did not see the incident and called it a "serious matter" for the citing commissioner. He added that Coombes appeared to change his mind midway through the accusation, and that he could see nothing himself.
Rugby.copy:
Munster head coach Clayton McMillan has backed Gavin Coombes after the number eight alleged he had been grabbed in the groin during Saturday's 24-18 defeat by Leinster. Coombes alleged the incident happened with an unnamed Leinster player at a ruck towards the end of the first half of the United Rugby Championship derby at the Aviva Stadium.

Coombes raised the allegation with match referee Andrew Brace, but the television match official (TMO), Colin Stanley, could not find any video evidence of the incident. Speaking after the game, McMillan backed Coombes and, referencing the citing commissioner who can punish retrospective incidents after a review, said it was something that had to be left "for the powers that be".

bullets: England head coach Steve Borthwick is reportedly considering a surprise call-up for Newcastle Red Bulls forward Max Hicks ahead of the Nations Championship, according to The Times. The 26-year-old, who previously played for the Māori All Blacks and Super Rugby's Highlanders, has impressed in the Gallagher PREM and can play at lock or blindside flanker.

Hicks's Māori All Blacks appearances do not prevent him from playing for England, although any selection would be subject to eligibility confirmation. England already have depth in the back five of the scrum, including Maro Itoje, Ollie Chessum and George Martin, but injuries and the demands of the Gallagher PREM and Nations Championship could create openings. His physicality and versatility are the qualities said to appeal to Borthwick.

bullets: Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend received a boost as Huw Jones, Blair Kinghorn and Tom Jordan all returned from injury at the weekend, ahead of Monday's Nations Championship squad announcement. Jones scored his first try for Toulon in a 41-20 win over Pau, having missed their Challenge Cup victory over Edinburgh. Kinghorn started at fly-half for Toulouse after more than a month out, kicking three conversions in 62 minutes of a 38-33 win over Perpignan.

Jordan played the full 80 minutes at full-back as Bristol Bears beat Exeter Chiefs 20-7, having missed their previous two matches with an unspecified muscle strain. Scotland open their Nations Championship campaign against the All Blacks on 7 November, then face Australia on 15 November and Japan on 21 November at Murrayfield. Those results will determine their opponents for finals weekend at Twickenham on the final weekend of November.
Rugby.copy:

Jones had missed the French side's victory over Edinburgh in the Challenge Cup last weekend but returned to the 13 jersey and crossed for a crucial effort just before half-time as Toulon ran out 41-20 winners at the Stade Felix Mayol.

Munster led through a Shane Daly try and eight points from 20-year-old fly-half Charlie O'Shea. Tommy O'Brien then scored before half-time from a Jamison Gibson-Park pass. Second-half tries from Ryan Baird and Charlie Tector put Leinster ahead, and Jamie Osborne's late score secured the bonus point.

Ben O'Connor crossed in the final minute to earn Munster a losing bonus point. Gibson-Park, one of 11 British and Irish Lions in Leinster's starting line-up, made three try assists. Leinster travel to Connacht on Friday (19:45 GMT) and Munster host the Sharks at Thomond Park on Saturday (17:30). The two sides' internationals then enter Ireland camp ahead of November's Nations Championship fixtures.

However, Tommy O'Brien hit back for Leinster before half-time after being set up by fit-again scrum-half Jamison Gibson-Park, who notched three try assists in an eye-catching display.

Rugby.summary: Ireland score six tries to beat South Africa in the first of two WXV Global Series meetings in Cape Town.
bullets: Ireland beat South Africa with six tries in the first of two WXV Global Series meetings in Cape Town, marking their first trip to South Africa. Aoife Dalton, Linda Djougang and Jane Clohessy scored in the first half to give Ireland a narrow interval lead, with Beibhinn Parsons, captain Erin King and a second Djougang try following after the break.

Ireland lost their WXV opener to the United States before beating Japan, and will aim to finish the campaign with a third win from four games when they meet South Africa again in Cape Town on 31 October (13:00 GMT). The sides' only previous meeting was a 2006 Women's Rugby World Cup match in Canada, which Ireland won 37-0. Ireland made 13 handling errors, but fly-half Dannah O'Brien's goal-kicking proved the difference in the first half.
Rugby.copy:
Ireland scored six tries to mark their first trip to South Africa with victory over the Springboks in the first of two WXV Global Series meetings in Cape Town. Aoife Dalton, Linda Djougang and Jane Clohessy crossed to give Ireland a slender half-time lead at the end of a ding-dong opening period in which Aseza Hele, Vainah Ubisi and Maria Tshiremba scored for the hosts.

Beibhinn Parsons and captain Erin King - who was sin-binned in the first half for a high tackle - extended Ireland's lead in the second half before Lerato Makua hit back for the Springboks.

Rugby.copy:
The WXV Global Series fixture between Japan and Wales was brought to a halt during the second half following a serious injury sustained by Freya Bell. Proceedings were suspended for over six minutes, with medical personnel from both sides treating the Wales player on the field at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium in Tokyo. At 52 minutes and with Wales ahead 7-0, centre Bell collapsed clutching her leg following a clear-out at a ruck.

Play initially carried on around her as she remained on the ground gripping her leg in visible distress, with a Wales medic attending to her. The referee subsequently called a stoppage, allowing Bell to receive treatment.

Rugby.summary: Fiji Shows Character To Defeat Japan 34–28 In Thrilling Test Match Fiji Rugby Union
Rugby.copy:
The Fiji Water Flying Fijians produced a courageous and disciplined performance to defeat Japan 34–28 in a thrilling international Test match, overcoming the challenge of playing 20 minutes with 14 men to secure a memorable victory on Japanese soil.

In a contest that was evenly poised at 21–21 at halftime, Fiji demonstrated resilience, tactical discipline and composure under pressure to outlast the Brave Blossoms and deliver a winning start for newly appointed head coach Jake White.

Rugby.title: Wales grind out frustrating WXV win against Japan
Rugby.summary: Wales earn a three-try victory against Japan in tricky Tokyo conditions to secure a second win of their WXV campaign.
bullets: Wales beat Japan in Tokyo to secure a second victory of their WXV campaign, in swirling wind, rain and humidity between the sides ranked 11th and 12th in the world. The first half looked likely to end scoreless until scrum-half Seren Lockwood scored in the 35th minute to give Wales a 7-0 lead at the break. Replacement Kelsey Jones drove over from a lineout, and Lockwood added a second try at the death.

Wales lost centre Freya Bell to a serious-looking knee injury during the match. The report described the performance as far from impressive, but said Sean Lynn's side had shown they can win ugly, with the bench making the difference. The two sides meet again in Kumagaya City next Saturday.
Rugby.copy:
Wales ground out a win over Japan in tricky Tokyo conditions to secure a second victory of their WXV campaign. Swirling wind, rain and humidity made for a real battle between sides ranked 11th and 12th in the world, with a scrappy first-half looking likely to end scoreless.

But scrum-half Seren Lockwood's 35th-minute snipe gave the game a much-needed spark and the visitors a 7-0 advantage at the break. Wales lost centre Freya Bell to a serious-looking knee injury, but the impact of the bench proved the difference as Kelsey Jones drove over off a lineout ball, before Lockwood finished a rare moment of class at the death.

Rugby.title: No panic for England but Mitchell issues PWR warning
Rugby.summary: A 2-0 series defeat for the Red Roses, their record 39-match winning streak and 41-match unbeaten run ended, and consecutive losses for the first time since 2016 - England are not invincible.
Rugby.copy:
Before England's three-match series against Canada, few would have predicted this outcome. A 2-0 series defeat for the Red Roses; their record 39-match winning streak and 41-match unbeaten run – stretching back nearly four years – ended; and consecutive losses for the first time since 2016.

Over the past 13 months, Canada have turned a 33-13 defeat in the World Cup final into a statement 31-22 win in Ottawa. And three years out from the 2029 World Cup, they have laid down an early marker of their title credentials.

Rugby.title: Red Roses suffer back-to-back defeats for first time in 10 years as Canada make statement
Rugby.summary: Red Roses suffer back-to-back defeats for first time in 10 years as Canada make statement The Guardian
bullets: England's Red Roses lost 31-22 to Canada in Ottawa in the WXV Global Series, their first consecutive defeats in a decade and only their third loss in 74 matches. Canada captain Sophie de Goede, the reigning world player of the year, scored a hat-trick, and Savannah Bauder also crossed. England replied through Maddie Feaunati, Amy Cokayne and Emma Sing, having trailed 12-7 at half-time.

England captain Meg Jones said the team is 'not broken, we just need to grow'. Head coach John Mitchell criticised the lack of a connection between referee Aurélie Groizeleau and the television match official. England finish the WXV series against the USA next Friday, while Canada's next games are slated for the 2027 Pacific Four tournament.
Rugby.copy:
History-makers, era-enders, giant-slayers. Breaking England’s unbeaten run was a statement for Canada last Friday but they backed it up in a 31-22 win to deal the Red Roses their first consecutive loss in a decade, sending a formidable message to the rest of world rugby.

Some may view it as too early to call but Canada are serious contenders for the World Cup trophy in 2029, especially if they progress at the same rate that their performances have improved in just a year from that World Cup final loss to England in 2025.

Rugby.title: Canada inflict back-to-back losses on England
Rugby.summary: England suffer back-to-back defeats for the first time in a decade as Canada win 31-22 in Ottawa, including a hat-trick for captain Sophie de Goede.
bullets: England lost 31-22 to Canada in the WXV Series in Ottawa, their first back-to-back defeats in a decade. Canada scored five tries to England's three, including a hat-trick from captain Sophie de Goede. It followed Canada's 24-21 win in Toronto last weekend, which ended the Red Roses' 41-match unbeaten run, and gave Canada a 2-0 series win after a 26-26 draw in Exeter in September.

Head coach John Mitchell said England had become "a little bit predictable" and need a "new stimulus" in the new year. He also called for improved officiating standards after there was no television match official connection in the stadium, saying Jess Breach's disallowed interception try was a turning point. England face the USA in New Jersey next Friday, hoping to avoid three straight defeats for the first time since 2013.
Rugby.copy:
Head coach John Mitchell said England need a "new stimulus" after losing 31-22 to Canada in the WXV Series in Ottawa to suffer back-to-back defeats for the first time in a decade.

The hosts ran in five tries to England's three, including a hat-trick for captain Sophie de Goede, as they backed up last weekend's 24-21 win in Toronto, which ended the Red Roses' 41-match unbeaten streak, with another statement victory.

Rugby.title: Impressive Gloucester beat Bath to extend lead at top of Prem
Rugby.summary: Gloucester storm to their first win over Bath in the Prem at Kingsholm since April 2022 with a 23-5 victory built on an immense defensive display.
Rugby.copy:
Gloucester stormed to their first win over Bath in the Prem at Kingsholm since April 2022 with a 23-5 victory built on an immense defensive display. The Cherry and Whites were down to 13 men for a period of the first half but led 9-5 at half-time, having repelled wave after wave of Bath pressure on their tryline.

George Barton then kicked three successive penalties to put the hosts 9-0 up before Kepu Tuipulotu pulled a try back just before the break from a driving maul. Freddie Thomas scored under the posts to stretch Gloucester's lead further midway through the second half and Max Llewellyn had Kingsholm raucous when he rolled over with two minutes to go for a famous victory that reaffirms their status as league leaders.

Rugby.title: Wade equals Ashton's Prem try-scoring record as Newcastle beat Sale
Rugby.summary: Christian Wade equals Chris Ashton's Prem try-scoring record with a 101st score as Newcastle post their first league win of their season against Sale.
bullets: Christian Wade equalled Chris Ashton's Premiership try-scoring record with his 101st try, scored in the right corner nine minutes into the second half. Newcastle Red Bulls beat Sale Sharks 17-3 at Kingston Park for their first league win of the season, with hooker George McGuigan adding a second try from a maul just after the hour.

The result was only Newcastle's fifth win in four Premiership seasons and leaves Harlequins as the only side yet to win this season. Sale, unbeaten in their previous two league games, scored only a George Ford penalty in blustery conditions. Newcastle coach Dan McFarland said there was no turning point and called it a long journey, adding that Wade deserves to take the record.
Rugby.copy:
Christian Wade equalled Chris Ashton's Prem try-scoring record with a 101st score as Newcastle Red Bulls posted their first league win of their season against Sale Sharks. On a blustery night dominated by kicking, penalties and stubborn defence, the match delivered a 17-3 win for the hosts and the try that Kingston Park wanted, with Wade going over in the right corner to draw level with Ashton nine minutes into the second period.

While a second eluded Wade in a game of few chances, George McGuigan managed to smuggle the ball over at the back of a maul as Newcastle stretched clear to post only a fifth win in four Prem seasons.

Rugby.title: Wallaroos complete Scotland sweep as retiring Smith gets standing ovation despite red
Rugby.summary: Wallaroos complete Scotland sweep as retiring Smith gets standing ovation despite red The Guardian
Rugby.copy:
The Wallaroos completed their three-game sweep over Scotland with a 38-31 win on Friday in a spicy contest that featured biting accusations and a string of yellow cards. Australia produced plenty of classy moments in Canberrabut again lacked discipline in tackles and around the ruck to keep the tourists in it. The hosts received four yellow cards, with the retiring centre Cecilia Smith earning two of those to finish her 34-Test career on a red.

Scotland had two players sent to the sin bin and it could have been far uglier if the Wallaroos centre Georgina Friedrichs’ accusations of biting had been verified on review. But the officials saw no evidence and there were no bite marks on Friedrich’s forearm, so the referee waved the complaints away.

Racket.title: Dart stuns Badosa to make second career semi-final
Racket.summary: Harriet Dart reaches the second WTA Tour semi-final of her career as she fights back from a set down to beat Paula Badosa in the Guangzhou Open.
Racket.copy:
Britain's Harriet Dart reached the second WTA Tour semi-final of her career when she fought back from a set down to beat fifth seed Paula Badosa at the Guangzhou Open in China.

The 30-year-old triumphed 3-6 6-2 6-4 against Spain's Badosa - ranked 54 places above her - in two hours and 15 minutes at Nansha International Tennis Centre. Dart's first appearance in the semi-finals of a tour event was in the Transylvania Open in Cluj-Napoca, where she lost in straight sets to Karolina Pliskova.

Racket.title: Guangzhou Open: Harriet Dart reaches second WTA Tour semi-final of career
Racket.summary: Guangzhou Open: Harriet Dart reaches second WTA Tour semi-final of career BBC
bullets: Britain's Harriet Dart reached the second WTA Tour semi-final of her career at the Guangzhou Open, coming from a set down to beat fifth seed Paula Badosa 3-6 6-2 6-4 in two hours and 15 minutes. The 30-year-old, who came through qualifying and beat second seed Janice Tjen in the previous round, will face 16-year-old Chinese wildcard Sun Xinran in the last four on Saturday.

Dart, who reached a career high of 70th in 2024, has been outside the top 100 for most of the past two seasons, but the run puts her on the cusp of a return and a possible direct place in the Australian Open main draw in January. She has won 17 of 22 tour-level hard-court matches since Wimbledon, and has worked with former Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli since earlier this year.

Racket.title: Shock Basel loss dents Djokovic's ATP Finals hopes
Racket.summary: Novak Djokovic's hopes of reaching the ATP Finals in Turin next month fade with a surprise defeat by Jan-Lennard Struff in Basel.
bullets: Novak Djokovic's hopes of a record 19th ATP Finals appearance were dented by a 6-7 (4-7) 7-5 7-6 (7-5) defeat to Jan-Lennard Struff at the Swiss Indoors in Basel. The 39-year-old, playing the tournament for the first time in 15 years, had never previously lost to Struff in nine meetings. He is now 11th in the standings, outside the top 10 for the first time since 2018.

The year's top eight qualify for the event in Turin, and Rafael Jodar holds the final spot in ninth because world number one Jannik Sinner is injured. Djokovic trails Jodar by 319 points and can still gain ground at the Paris Masters in November. Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton have confirmed places for the finals from 15 to 22 November. Shelton lost to wildcard Jerome Kym in Basel.
Racket.copy:
Novak Djokovic's hopes of making a record 19th appearance at the ATP Finals have been dented by a surprise defeat against Jan-Lennard Struff at the Swiss Indoors in Basel. Playing in the tournament for the first time in 15 years, the 39-year-old lost 6-7 (4-7) 7-5 7-6 (7-5) - the first time he has been beaten by Struff in nine meetings.

"I knew I needed to go for it. There was only one way to play it. So, I was very, very happy," said the world number 27. "I knew I had to play my best tennis to have a chance. The last eight times he beat me very, very easily. So, I'm very, very happy and pleased with the performance."

Racket.title: Rybakina withdraws from Tokyo, Fernandez advances to semifinals
Racket.summary: Rybakina withdraws from Tokyo, Fernandez advances to semifinals WTA Tennis
Racket.copy:
World No. 1 Elena Rybakina withdrew from the Toray Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo on Friday because of a neck injury, handing Leylah Fernandez a walkover into the semifinals. In a statement released, Rybakina said she was dealing with inflammation and pain in her neck.

"Dear fans, I’m very sorry to announce that I’ve had to withdraw from my next match," Rybakina said in the statement. "Unfortunately, I’ve been experiencing inflammation and pain in my neck, which has been affecting my ability to play at my best. It’s a very difficult decision, as I love playing here and always appreciate the incredible support from the fans. I hope to be back again next year. Thank you all for your understanding and support."

Racket.title: Alcaraz repels Basilashvili’s 4 set points in Vienna, books QF spot
Racket.summary: Alcaraz repels Basilashvili’s 4 set points in Vienna, books QF spot ATP Tour
Racket.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz earned a victory of two starkly contrasting halves to reach his 60th tour-level quarter-final on Thursday at the Erste Bank Open. The No. 3 player in the PIF ATP Rankings, Alcaraz held off a second-set resurgence from Nikoloz Basilashvili to claim a 6-1, 7-6(11) triumph in Vienna. Basilashvili entered the clash having won 14 of his past 17 matches and recovered from a difficult start to hand Alcaraz a stern test, but the Spaniard raised his level in trademark fashion just when he needed it for a one-hour, 41-minute win.

Alcaraz had reeled off seven consecutive games from 1-1 in the first set to take complete control of Thursday’s encounter inside the Wiener Stadthalle, producing some typically showstopping all-court tennis. But he then let slip a break lead in the second set as last week’s Almaty finalist Basilashvili dug deep, and was forced to save four set points in the subsequent tie-break before converting his fourth match point for his 23rd consecutive win at ATP 500 level.

bullets: Double Olympic medallist PV Sindhu reached the women's singles quarter-finals of the Hylo Open Super 500 on Thursday, beating France's Rosy Oktavia Pancasari 21-9, 21-6 in 26 minutes. Fellow Indians Malvika Bansod and Isharani Baruah went out: Malvika lost 11-21, 17-21 to Canada's Wen Yu Zhang in 31 minutes, and Isharani lost 14-21, 19-21 to eighth seed Line Hojmark Kjaersfeldt of Denmark in 39 minutes. Racket.summary: Novak Djokovic pulls off a hard-fought comeback victory over Ugo Humbert to keep alive his hopes of qualifying for the season-ending ATP Finals.
Racket.copy:
Novak Djokovic pulled off a hard-fought comeback victory over Ugo Humbert on his first appearance in Basel for 15 years. Battling in the final months of the year to keep alive his chances of qualifying for the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin, Djokovic celebrated what he viewed as a "big win" by overcoming Frenchman Ugo Humbert 4-6 6-3 6-4.

The men's record 24-time major winner blasted a forehand winner down the line to end the contest after two and a half hours. It ensured Djokovic, 11th in the race to Turin, remains in the hunt for a record 19th appearance at the ATP Finals, for which only the year's top eight performers qualify.

What started as pins and needles in his arm became increasingly painful before scans revealed serious bone stress. Racket.summary: The Swiss legend has reflected after playing the final match of his career. The post What Stan Wawrinka said after his emotional farewell at Swiss Indoors in Basel appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: Stan Wawrinka retired from tennis after a 7-5, 7-6(2) first-round loss to Jiri Lehecka at the 2026 Swiss Indoors in Basel on Tuesday night. The 41-year-old Swiss, a three-time Grand Slam champion and former world No 3, began his career in 2002.

Speaking afterwards, Wawrinka said his farewell was much more beautiful than he could have dreamed and that he had no regrets, having always given 100% in every match. He said he felt competitive in his final year, and that saying goodbye at each tournament had been sad. Finishing in Switzerland, with a ceremony the previous day, was an ideal ending. He added that after his major injuries, his body and head no longer followed as they once did.
Racket.copy:
Stan Wawrinka described his farewell from tennis as “much more beautiful than I could have dreamed” after playing the last match of his career at the 2026 Swiss Indoors. The three-time Grand Slam champion retired after a 7-5, 7-6(2) loss to Jiri Lehecka in the first round in Basel on Tuesday night.

Wawrinka firmly established himself as one of the most popular players on the ATP Tour during an outstanding career than started in 2002. Speaking to ATPTour.com, Wawrinka revealed he has “no regrets” when asked about his legacy.

bullets: Stan Wawrinka retired at 41 after a 7-5 7-6 (7-2) defeat by Czech Jiri Lehecka in front of home fans in Basel on Tuesday, ending a professional career of 23 years and 985 matches. The former world number three won three Grand Slam titles: the 2014 Australian Open, the 2015 French Open and the 2016 US Open.

He beat Novak Djokovic in the finals of the 2015 French Open and 2016 US Open, and Rafael Nadal in the 2014 Australian Open final. He also spent 267 weeks in the top 10, won one Masters 1000 title and 15 other tour-level titles. Wawrinka said he wanted to give everything with no regrets and that at some point you have to close the book, while Djokovic called him a "legend".
Racket.copy:
Whether through technique or toil, Stan Wawrinka has always been able to whip fans into a frenzy. The ability to stir the emotions of a crowd never left him - even in what proved to be the final tour-level match of the 41-year-old Swiss star's glorious career.

Former world number three Wawrinka might have lost to Czech opponent Jiri Lehecka in front of passionate home support in Basel on Tuesday, but he did not wave farewell without showing the hallmarks of a stunning career that exceeded expectations.

Since 2024, the Global Sport for Good Initiative has brought together four international sports federations – World Rugby, FIBA (Basketball), World Athletics and BWF (Badminton) – and the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to develop and harness the role that sport participation has in enhancing wellbeing, inclusion and community development globally.

The Global Sport for Good Initiative aims to strengthen programmes across World Rugby and partner international federations, broaden participation in sport, and increase its contribution to resilient communities, health and wellbeing, education and inclusion. To achieve these outcomes, World Rugby, the IOC and partner federations are placing community players’ needs at the centre of sport delivery, embedding this approach in grassroots coach education and workforce development, and improving how they measure and demonstrate impact.

bullets: Jannik Sinner will begin working with former world No 2 Magnus Norman at the end of the 2026 season, according to a report in The Times. Norman takes over from Darren Cahill, who has been part of the Italian's team since July 2022 and, alongside Simone Vagnozzi, helped him win five major titles. Norman is free to join because Stan Wawrinka retires at the end of this season.

Norman, runner-up at the 2000 French Open, previously coached Robin Soderling to back-to-back Roland Garros finals in 2009 and 2010. He also guided Wawrinka to three Grand Slam titles. Sinner successfully defended Wimbledon this year but has not played since beating Alexander Zverev, because of a knee injury. According to The Times, five-time Grand Slam winner Sinner will start working with former player Magnus Norman at the end of the 2026 season with the Swede taking over from Darren Cahill.

Norman is a former world No 2 who finished runner-up at the 2000 French Open and he has enjoyed great success as a coach, as he mentored Robin Soderling in 2009 and 2010 and during that period his fellow Swede reached back-to-back French Open finals.

Racket.title: ATP doubles proposals: Players and legends sign open letter to prevent cuts
Racket.summary: ATP doubles proposals: Players and legends sign open letter to prevent cuts BBC
bullets: More than 150 men's doubles players, including British world number one Henry Patten and the Bryan brothers, have signed an open letter urging the ATP Tour to rethink proposals that would cut draw sizes and reduce prize money from 2028. The letter was signed on Monday by 137 current players, 28 legends and 20 national federations. The ATP has proposed halving doubles draws at Masters 1000 events to 16 teams, with smaller tournaments cut to eight teams, and the share of prize money going to doubles could fall from 20% to 10%.

The ATP board, made up of chairman Andrea Gaudenzi, four tournament representatives and four player representatives, will vote on the proposals at the ATP Finals in Turin next month. The ATP says the changes are based on data-led analysis of costs, revenue and viewership, and ATP sources insist a compromise is likely. Mike and Bob Bryan said they would support legal action, as in their 2005 lawsuit against the ATP over planned doubles changes.

Racket.summary: Jannik Sinner, Alexander Zverev earn over $1 million each in ATP’s record $18.3 million payout as Novak D The Times of India
bullets: Jannik Sinner and Alexander Zverev were the biggest beneficiaries of the ATP Tour's record $18.3m profit-sharing payout for the 2024 season, each earning more than $1m from Masters 1000 events. The ATP finalised the distribution on 3 October 2025, with 186 players who earned ranking points at the nine events qualifying. Sinner received $1,333,770 and Zverev $1,228,472, ahead of Andrey Rublev on $698,474.

The payout was 2.7 times the $6.6m distributed for 2023, while Novak Djokovic finished 12th with $403,641, outside the top 10. Under the 50-50 model introduced in 2022, profits above base prize money at Masters 1000 events are split equally between players and tournaments. The payments are separate from prize money and the $20.5m fixed bonus pool for the top 30 players.
Racket.copy:
Jannik Sinner and Alexander Zverev emerged as the biggest beneficiaries of the ATP Tour's record profit-sharing payout for the 2024 season, with the two stars earning more than $1 million each from the Masters 1000 events. Novak Djokovic, meanwhile, finished outside the top 10 in the profit-sharing standings despite another productive season on the tour.

The ATP finalised the distribution of its record $18.3 million profit-sharing pool on October 3, 2025, completing the total compensation package for players who competed at Masters 1000 tournaments in 2024. A total of 186 players who earned PIF ATP Rankings points at the nine events qualified for a share of the payout.

bullets: An Se-young won the women's singles title at the Yonex French Open 2026 on Sunday 25 October, beating India's Pusarla Venkata Sindhu 16-21, 21-11, 21-12 in the final at the Arena Grand Paris. The world No. 1 extended her winning streak to 50 matches, claimed a 10th title of the season and secured a third consecutive French Open crown, her fourth overall. She has won 66 of 67 matches this year.

The streak began after a 2-0 loss to China's Wang Zhiyi in the All England Open final in March. An played through an injury near her right Achilles tendon, sustained in the Denmark Open final, which medical examinations showed was not serious. She is expected to enter about three more tournaments this year, including the BWF World Tour Finals, and two more titles would beat her own single-season record of 11. She holds 48 career titles, past Susi Susanti's 46.

bullets: Christo Popov won the Yonex French Open 2026 men's singles title on Sunday, becoming the first French player to win the crown and reaching the world No. 1 ranking for the first time in his career. Racket.title: Malaysian badminton makes Super 750 history at French Open [WATCH]
Racket.summary: Malaysian badminton makes Super 750 history at French Open [WATCH] NST Online
bullets: Malaysia will contest a record three finals at the French Open at Arena Grand Paris, the first time it has reached three finals at a single Super 750 event since the category began in 2018. Its previous best was two. In an all-Malaysian men's doubles final, world No. 11 Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun face world No. 5 Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani, guaranteeing a first Malaysian title since 2004.

Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah, world No. 4, face Japan's world No. 3 Yuki Fukushima-Mayu Matsumoto in the women's doubles, seeking successive World Tour titles after winning in Denmark last week. They beat Rin Iwanaga-Kie Nakanishi 21-17, 22-20 in the semi-finals. In the mixed doubles, world No. 31 Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing meet China's top seeds Feng Yan Zhe-Huang Dong Ping, who beat them in the China Masters final last month.
Racket.copy:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will contest a record three finals at the French Open later today, with one title already assured. Four pairs will carry the nation's challenge at Arena Grand Paris, marking the first time Malaysia has reached three event finals at a single Super 750 tournament since the category was introduced in 2018.

The country's previous best was two, achieved at the 2023 Denmark Open, last year's Japan Open, and last week's Denmark Open. Racket.title: An Se-young Dominates With 47th Title, Extends World No. 1 Reign
Racket.summary: An Se-young Dominates With 47th Title, Extends World No. 1 Reign 조선일보
bullets: The Badminton World Federation announced that An Se-young has set a record by winning her 47th international singles title, passing Indonesia's Susi Susanti, who won 46. The BWF's count covers only titles since 1999, when it began compiling statistics, and excludes team events such as the Uber Cup. An has won nine individual titles this season from 11 tournaments entered.

An has held the world number one ranking for 106 consecutive weeks, 168 in total, with 122,287 points. She has reached the semi-finals of the BWF World Tour France Open (Super 750) in Paris, beating China's Han Yue 21-13, 21-16 in the quarter-finals. A fourth French Open title would be her 10th of the year and the first three-peat at the event since Pi Hongyan won in 2003–2005.
Racket.copy:
[Sports Chosun Reporter Kim Ga-eul] Japan has praised An Se-young (Samsung Life Insurance), the "world's strongest," for her overwhelming skills. An Se-young is demonstrating formidable strength. She has won nine gold medals in individual events this season alone. Out of 11 international tournaments she participated in this season, she finished as runner-up at the All England Open, March, and withdrew in the round of 16 at the Japan Open, July, due to injury, but she claimed victory in all other events. An Se-young set a new record by reaching the top 11 times last year, tying the all-time single-season record for most wins in men's and women's singles with Kento Momota (Japan). At her current pace, she could set a new record.

The Badminton World Federation (BWF) officially announced, "An Se-young has set a new record by winning her 47th international singles title." The previous record was held by Indonesia's badminton "legend" Susi Susanti, who had 46 wins. However, the BWF's count of singles titles only includes records since 1999 when it began compiling statistics. Additionally, team event results such as the Uber Cup (World Women's Team Badminton Championships) or the Asian Team Championships are excluded.

Men's world number five pair Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzudin Rumsani beat world number one pair Kim Won Ho-Seo Seung Jae of South Korea 21-15, 21-18 in 36 minutes.

Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun reached the last four after a walkover, as compatriots Aaron Chia-Soh Wooi Yik retired trailing 0-5 two minutes into the first game, with no official reason given. Malaysia has not won the men's doubles title since Gan Teik Chai-Koo Kien Keat in 2004. In the mixed doubles, Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing face China's world number six pair Guo Xin Wai-Chen Fang Hui in the semi-finals.
Racket.copy:
This is a record achievement at the prestigious BWF World Tour Super 750 championships. And history beckons for world No 4 Pearly Tan-M Thinaah, who could add a second title being the only Malaysian women’s doubles pair to have won the crown in the tournament’s 117-year history, in 2022.

In the last eight match early this morning, the Malaysian pair defeated world No 9 pair Bulgarian sisters Gabriela Stoeva-Stefani Stoeva with a comfortable score of 21-12, 21-15 in a match that took 39 minutes.

Golf.title: Mexico Open: Karl Vilips shoots 62 to take the first-round lead with Marco Penge two shots back
Golf.summary: Mexico Open: Karl Vilips shoots 62 to take the first-round lead with Marco Penge two shots back Sky Sports
Golf.copy:
Karl Vilips used two long birdie streaks to take the first-round lead Thursday in the Mexico Open, the first of two straight PGA Tour events in the country. Vilips shot a nine-under 62 in the afternoon round on the Vidanta Vallarta layout, making five straight birdies on Nos. 11-15 on his opening nine and finishing with four in a row. In between, he had another birdie and a bogey.

The 25-year-old Australian pointed to his driver. "Had it on a string for the first nine," Vilips said. "Got a little loose in the middle and got it back on course toward the end of the round. It was lift, clean and place today so being in the fairway was a must for me and I took advantage of those drives that I hit."

Golf.title: Why LIV Golf's latest crisis could have an unexpected Scottish upside
Golf.summary: Why LIV Golf's latest crisis could have an unexpected Scottish upside The Herald
Golf.copy:
Four years after LIV Golf turned the men’s professional game upside down, the question is no longer which stars it might lure away with Saudi riches, but whether the breakaway circuit can keep enough of them to survive.

After filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September, LIV is now trying to secure enough players and financial backing to launch a revamped version of the competition in 2027. That task has become harder as a stream of prominent players head for the exit. Jon Rahm, Adrian Meronk, David Puig, Louis Oosthuizen and Ian Poulter have all said their farewells.

Golf.title: Sergio Garcia to play on DP World Tour after joining LIV Golf exodus
Golf.summary: Sergio Garcia to play on DP World Tour after joining LIV Golf exodus The Japan Times
bullets: Former Masters champion Sergio Garcia has confirmed he will return to the DP World Tour next season, joining the exodus from LIV Golf. The 46-year-old Spaniard captained Fireballs GC after leaving the PGA Tour for LIV in 2022, winning in Spain in 2024 and Hong Kong in 2025. He said he is also keeping his options open for a PGA Tour return, and earlier this autumn asked a federal judge to terminate his LIV deal.

LIV filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in September and hopes to continue under a "LIV 2.0" plan after the Saudi Public Investment Fund withdrew its support. Others not returning include Jon Rahm, Tyrrell Hatton, Ian Poulter, Louis Oosthuizen and Graeme McDowell. Garcia, a nine-time Ryder Cup participant, said he wants to return to the Masters in 2027 and make the European team at Adare Manor.
Golf.copy:
Former Masters champion Sergio Garcia joined the LIV Golf exodus on Thursday, confirming he plans to return to the DP World Tour. The 46-year-old Spaniard had served as the captain of the Fireballs GC team since leaving the PGA Tour for LIV Golf in 2022.

“Next season, I’ll be playing on the DP World Tour,” Garcia posted on social media. “This tour has been a huge part of my career from the very beginning, and I’m proud to call it home again. I’m also keeping my options open for a return to the PGA Tour. And probably the most exciting part for me is strengthening my personal relationships, both new and old.”

His departure from LIV Golf was already known after four years playing on the breakaway circuit.

"Next season, I'll be playing on the DP World Tour," Garcia wrote. "This tour has been a huge part of my career from the very beginning, and I'm proud to call it home again. "I'm also keeping my options open for a return to the PGA Tour. And probably the most exciting part for me is strengthening my personal relationships, both new and old."

Introduced in January 2017, the rule says players cannot hold the roles if they decline European Tour membership or fail to meet their minimum event obligation in any season.

Poulter and McDowell have declared themselves out of LIV 2.0 and could regain DP World Tour cards next season through Legends category status, but the captaincy roles remain out of reach. Garcia, 46, says he will return to the DP World Tour "without a doubt" and has told captain Luke Donald he will help as a player or vice-captain at Adare Manor. Justin Rose, Francesco Molinari and Rory McIlroy are now next in line as captains.

TG understands that a long-standing rule which effectively bans the likes of Sergio Garcia, Ian Poulter, Lee Westwood and Graeme McDowell from representing Europe as captains or vice-captains, is not expected to be changed in the near future to accommodate the returning greats.
